title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative:
All-China Federation of Trade Unions (ACFTU) has nearly 300 million members in more than 2.8 million grassroot trade union organizations, including 160 million members in non-public sectors and nearly 100 million members of migrant workers. The ACFTU is divided into 31 regional federations and 10 national industrial unions. Its 14th five-year plan has focused on:
• Safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of workers and enhancing their sense of fulfilment, happiness and security. • Establishing and improving a high-standard service system for workers and continuously increasing the quality of their life. • Building harmonious labour relations and promoting joint contribution, joint governance and sharing of social governance.
In respond to rapid development of new forms of employment in China, in particular platform employment, the ACFTU revised the Trade Union Law on 24 December 2021, with the aim to strengthen the rights of workers in new forms of employment to form unions. Innovative approaches are being explored to organize platform workers, and extend coverage of collective agreement to this working group.
Meanwhile the ACFTU has made efforts to address the shortage of skilled workers by exploring innovative skill-based collective bargaining, which has been developed and implemented in several cities within Zhejiang province.
In this biennium, ILO will provide support for ACFTU to enhance their capacity in protection of platform workers, collection of good practices on protection of platform workers. In addition, ILO will strengthen the collaboration with ACFTU on south-south and triangular cooperation (SSTC) to enhance the capacity of trade unions in Asia and Pacific to address emerging challenges in the world of work.
